{{Short description|South Korean mathematician and scholar}}
{{Distinguish|Kim Jong Un}}
'''Kim Yong-un''' ({{Langx|ko|김용운}}; 6 September 1927 – 30 May 2020) was a South Korean mathematician, philosopher, and critic of civilisations. He was active in various fields of mathematics, philosophy, anthropology, and linguistics, and is considered to have established the [[history of mathematics]] in Korea. He was a professor of mathematics at [[Hanyang University]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=1982-07-03|script-title=ko:광산김씨|url=https://news.joins.com/article/1642563|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[JoongAng Ilbo]]|language=ko}}</ref>

== Life ==
Kim Yong-un was born in [[Tokyo]], Japan in 1927.<ref>{{Cite web|last=임 |first=동근|date=2020-05-30|script-title=ko:한국 수학사 확립의 일등공신 김용운 교수 별세(종합)|url=https://www.yna.co.kr/view/AKR20200530047351011|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[Yonhap News Agency]]|language=ko}}</ref> He was liberated{{Clarify|reason=|date=July 2020}} in the year he entered [[Waseda University]] and returned to his father's hometown of [[Naju]], [[South Jeolla Province]] in 1946.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2018-08-19|script-title=ko:"북한은 '핵이란 독을 바른 토끼'…한반도 중립화 기회죠"|url=http://www.hani.co.kr/arti/culture/book/858267.html|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[The Hankyoreh]]|language=ko}}</ref> While working as a math teacher at Mokpo High School and [[Gwangju Jeil High School]] since 1947, he felt the need to popularize math and later wrote several popular math books.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|script-title=ko:수학자 김용운의 1백번째 저서 '카오스의 날개짓'-국민일보|url=http://news.kmib.co.kr/article/viewDetail.asp?newsClusterNo=01100201.19991101000001901|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[Kukmin Ilbo]]}}</ref> After teaching for more than 10 years, he earned a doctorate in science while studying in the [[United States]] and [[Canada]].<ref name=":0" />

In the late 1970s, he studied the history of mathematics, and since the 1980s, he has analyzed Korea and Japan in a comparative cultural way by combining mathematics and history.<ref name=":1" /> The original form, which means [[collective unconscious]]ness of the community, and the locality in which the community is located, were involved in the development of language and history.<ref name=":0" /> In 1983, he founded the Korean Mathematical History Association and became the first chairman, and in 1994, he participated in the development process of Ungjin Publishing (now Ungjin Thinkbig), a mathematics learning magazine brand of Ungjin Publishing (now Ungjin Thinkbig), along with his younger brother, Professor Kim Yong-guk of Hanyang University. This is also the predecessor of Thinkbig, a learning center brand of Ungjin.<ref>{{Cite web|script-title=ko:네이버 뉴스 라이브러리|url=https://newslibrary.naver.com/viewer/index.nhn?articleId=1994012100209113001&editNo=40&printCount=1&publishDate=1994-01-21&officeId=00020&pageNo=13&printNo=22406&publishType=00010|access-date=2020-06-29|website=NAVER Newslibrary}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2000-11-22|script-title=ko:[학습지 업체] 웅진씽크빅|url=https://news.joins.com/article/4000002|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[JoongAng Ilbo]]|language=ko}}</ref> He wrote more than 150 books throughout his life.

== Academic background ==

* Bachelor's degree in mining at Waseda University in Japan (dropout)
* Bachelor's degree in mathematics at [[Chosun University]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=2006-01-01|script-title=ko:[특별기고] 김용운 교수‥國格을 높여야 '한민족 르네상스' 이룬다|url=https://www.hankyung.com/society/article/2005123047731|access-date=2020-06-29|website=[[The Korea Economic Daily]]|language=ko}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=[OBS '명불허전'] 수학자 김용운 교수 "한중일 뿌리 깊은 갈등, 고대사에 그 답이 있다" - OBS경인TV|url=http://www.obsnews.co.kr/news/articleView.html?idxno=918380|access-date=2020-06-29|website=www.obsnews.co.kr| date=9 October 2015 |language=ko}}</ref>
* Graduate School of Orburn University in the U.S. (Bachelor of Science)
* Graduate School of [[University of Alberta]], Canada (Doctor of Science)

== Career ==

* Assistant Professor of [[University of Wisconsin System|University of Wisconsin]] (1962–1965)
* Visiting professor at [[Kobe University]] in Japan
* A visiting professor at [[University of Tokyo|Tokyo University]] in Japan
* Guest Professor of the Center for International Cultural Research in Japan
* Professor of Mathematics at Hanyang University (1969–1993)
* President of the Korean Mathematical History Society
* Professor emeritus of mathematics at Hanyang University (1994-current)
* Chairman of the Korea Broadcasting Culture Promotion Agency (2000–2003)
* Director of the Korean Mathematical and Cultural Institute
